solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Excellent example as writer of music embraces church

indicators.note: embraces says the first piece wraps itself around the second

parts.note: one who scores music, a composer or arranger, is a scorer

explanation.surface: A composer's work is praised as a fine example, with a church somehow involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as writer of music' describes a person who scores a piece, not a musical term; 'embraces' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, a sizzler or outstanding specimen of anything is called a scorcher, a corker.

clue.text: Flier succeeded with wangle — not half!

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

indicators.note: only half the word wangle is used, its first three letters

explanation.surface: A pilot fiddles their way through, but only partly; 'not half!' is also slang for 'definitely'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half!' looks like the slang exclamation; here it tells you to keep only half of 'wangle'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird is a flier, and this large white waterbird is one example.

clue.text: With no pressure move to capture small portion

indicators.note: With no says the pressure letter is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: to pounce is to spring forward to seize prey
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A predator springs at its prey with no force, catching only a little.
explanation.definitionFit: An imperial weight of about 28 grams, used figuratively for a tiny amount, as in 'not an ounce of sense'.

clue.text: Possibly try gal's craze — one looking ahead

indicators.note: Possibly suggests the letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Someone tries out a girl's latest fad, which happens to be fortune-telling.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortune-teller peering into a glass orb claims to see the future, so is one who looks ahead.

clue.text: Adaptable, she can exchange cheque for coins?

indicators.note: Adaptable says the following letters can be altered into a new form

explanation.surface: A flexible woman can swap a cheque for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn a cheque into money is to cash it in; the question mark admits coins are only one form of cash.

clue.text: Smug person, greedy one — about right

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: a glutton is called a pig

explanation.surface: Character sketch of someone self-satisfied and greedy, roughly correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-righteous, priggish prude is smug about their own correctness.

clue.text: After upcoming editor brought in, backs lecturers

indicators.note: brought in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: rears are backs, the hind parts

indicators.note: in a down clue, upcoming says the letters climb, so they are read backwards

explanation.surface: A newly arriving editor joins the staff, supported by the teaching faculty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upcoming' reverses the abbreviation because this is a down clue; 'brought in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: In British universities a reader is a senior academic rank just below professor, so readers are lecturers.

clue.text: Favour sentimental stuff, dulcet in the extreme, on vessel

parts.note: goo is sickly sentimentality

indicators.note: in the extreme says to take the outermost letters of the word dulcet

parts.note: an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: A sweet, sentimental message delivered on board a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind deed done for someone, a helpful act, is a favour.

clue.text: Suitable for scamming? Very well!

definitions.meaning: read literally: apt as a swindle, a fiddle being a scam
in excellent health, the idiom for being in top condition

explanation.surface: Is this suitable for a con? Excellent!
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes the idiom word by word: fit (suitable) as a fiddle (a fraud).
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in perfect health, and literally it can be read as appropriate for a swindle.

clue.text: Bother man, non-Tory, on regular basis

indicators.note: on regular basis says to take every other letter, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: Pester a man who isn't a Conservative, routinely.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: To pester or irritate someone is to bother them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Port fashionable in the past

parts.note: chic means stylish or fashionable
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: A wine or harbour that was once trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' tempts as the drink; it is a harbour city on Lake Michigan.
explanation.definitionFit: This US city on Lake Michigan is a major inland port for shipping.

clue.text: Man sent tweet off? Writings from much earlier

indicators.note: off suggests the letters have gone wrong and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A man fires off a social-media post, set against ancient scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: The second part of the Christian Bible is a body of writings about two thousand years old.

clue.text: Cold king associated with economy — that's definite

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
Lear is Shakespeare's tragic king
a cut is an economy, a saving

explanation.surface: A chilly monarch is linked with spending cuts, and that's settled.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unambiguous or plain is clear-cut, beyond doubt.

clue.text: Arrogant and noisily changing third letter

indicators.note: changing third letter says the letter in third position of the word is swapped for another

parts.note: loudly means noisily

explanation.surface: Someone haughty is loudly altering a character in a word.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not name the replacement letter: changing the third letter of LOUDLY to R gives a real word meaning arrogant.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaving like a lord, haughty and high-handed, is a synonym for arrogant.

clue.text: Split, make changes over stretch of turbulent water

parts.note: to rip is to split or tear

indicators.note: in a down clue, over says the word is turned back to front

parts.note: to edit is to make changes to text

explanation.surface: Tear it up, revise it all, over a rough patch of sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong offshore current where tides meet creates a rough stretch of sea.

clue.text: Dictator recalled in Marmara Sea chronicle

indicators.note: recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tyrant remembered in a history of the Sea of Marmara, near Istanbul.
explanation.walkthrough: No word signals the hiding; 'recalled' does double duty, the letters lying backwards across 'Marmara Sea chronicle'.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius, the Roman general, was made dictator for life before his assassination.

clue.text: Shed in field not being moving

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow or field

indicators.note: moving says the letters of the word not shift into another order

explanation.surface: A shed out in a field that, oddly, isn't being moved.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple shed built against a wall with a sloping roof is a classic small outbuilding.

clue.text: Characters in chintz are in such order

definitions.text: Characters in chintz are in such order

parts.words: Characters in chintz are in such order
parts.note: the letters of chintz, C H I N T Z, run in the order they come in the alphabet

explanation.surface: A remark about the letters of a fabric's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' means letters, not people; check C, H, I, N, T, Z.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters arranged as A to Z are in the order of the letters, as in a dictionary.

clue.text: Initially appearing lively, outgoing, now extremely solitary

indicators.note: Initially says to take the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A person who first seemed lively and sociable is now very lonely.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on one's own, without company, is being solitary.

clue.text: Some prefer northern plant

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Certain gardeners favour a plant from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowerless green plant with feathery fronds is one kind of plant.

clue.text: Charlie greeting thin foreigner

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
hi is a greeting
lean means thin

explanation.surface: Charlie says hello to a skinny visitor from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from a South American country is, to a Briton, a foreigner, so a vague but fair example.

clue.text: Peace campaigner having crossed river, acted as chauffeur

indicators.note: having crossed says the first piece goes across, straddling, the second

parts.note: a dove is a political advocate of peace

explanation.surface: A pacifist crosses a river, working as a driver.
explanation.definitionFit: A chauffeur's job is to drive, so this past tense is what one did.

clue.text: Primarily treacly, tiny, over-pretty

indicators.note: Primarily says to take the first letter of the word after it

parts.note: wee is Scottish for tiny

explanation.surface: Mainly sickly sweet, small, and too cute.
explanation.definitionFit: Affectedly dainty or quaint, excessively cute, is twee.

clue.text: After review one's free as predicted

indicators.note: After review suggests the letters have been reworked and come out in a new order

explanation.surface: Following an assessment, someone is released, just as expected.
explanation.definitionFit: Something predicted was seen in advance, anticipated beforehand.
